claim: The default pytest run excludes the connector tests from collection regardless of the working directory pytest is invoked from.
verify_against: pytest ini options in pyproject.toml and tests/conftest.py collect_ignore semantics
verify_hint: Check [tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts/testpaths in pyproject.toml and the collect_ignore assignment in tests/conftest.py against pytest's path resolution (relative --ignore is cwd-relative, collect_ignore is conftest-dir-relative)
prior_evidence: pyproject.toml:113 sets addopts = "--ignore=tests/connectors". Pytest's --ignore option values are turned into absolute paths relative to the current working directory (os.path.abspath in _pytest/main.py pytest_ignore_collect), not the rootdir. addopts are plain command-line args, so they get no rootdir resolution. From a cwd other than the repo root, e.g. running `pytest /repo` from elsewhere, the ignore resolves to <cwd>/tests/connectors and does not match, so the directory is collected. The claim 'regardless of the working directory' is therefore false. Only testpaths is rootdir-relative. This is from my knowledge of pytest, not an executed run.

claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: 3. The rewritten test in `tests/unit/test_memory_listing_consistency.py` no longer skips, but the branch that actually runs in CI proves very little. On a case-sensitive filesystem the test now creates a second, genuinely different directory and asserts that it gets a different cache entry, which is close to a tautology for a cache keyed on device and inode numbers. The behavior the test was written to protect, two spellings of one directory sharing an entry, is only reached on a case-insensitive filesystem, and CI never runs on one. The existing symlink test at lines 187-197 covers the real invariant, so nothing was lost, but the new branch adds maintenance cost without adding coverage. (raised by 2/5 agents)
